findings.title: AI search and retrieval crawlers blocked from root (PerplexityBot)
findings.evidence: Observed at https://pexels.com/robots.txt via robots_txt_parser_longest_match [2026-09-13T16:32:39Z]: robots.txt disallows root '/' for retrieval agents: PerplexityBot. These build the indexes AI answers are assembled from, or fetch a page live when a user asks about it, so the brand cannot be cited at all. Training-only crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider) are also blocked, which is a separate and legitimate licensing choice. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Allow AI search and user-triggered retrieval agents, even if training crawlers stay blocked.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: In robots.txt, allow OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot (search indexes) and ChatGPT-User, Claude-User and Perplexity-User (live user fetches). You can keep GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended and CCBot disallowed if you do not want your content used for model training -- the two decisions are independent.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves crawlability by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: Missing primary H1 heading on landing page
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.pexels.com/api/ via heading_structure_inspection [2026-09-13T16:32:39Z]: Page lacks a primary <h1> heading tag to establish core topic and orientation for arriving visitors. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a single <h1> heading tag at the top of the main content summarizing the page's purpose.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves orientation by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: Missing XML sitemap declared in robots.txt or available at /sitemap.xml
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.pexels.com/sitemap.xml via http_get_sitemap_check [2026-09-13T16:32:39Z]: Request to https://www.pexels.com/sitemap.xml did not return a valid sitemap and no 'Sitemap:' directive was found in robots.txt. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Publish an XML sitemap and declare its location in robots.txt.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Generate an XML sitemap for public indexable URLs and add 'Sitemap: https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml' to robots.txt.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves crawlability by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: Content images carry no text alternative, hiding any fact they display
findings.evidence:
Observed at https://www.pexels.com/api/ via image_alt_coverage_inspection [2026-09-13T16:32:39Z]: 7 of 25 images (28%) have no alt attribute at all (images correctly marked decorative with alt="" are excluded). Any figure, price, spec or claim rendered inside those images is unreadable to a retrieval bot. (Confidence: high)
Additional evidence (crawl-render-audit): Observed at https://www.pexels.com/become-a-partner/ via image_alt_coverage_inspection [2026-09-13T16:32:39Z]: 6 of 19 images (32%) have no alt attribute at all (images correctly marked decorative with alt="" are excluded). Any figure, price, spec or claim rendered inside those images is unreadable to a retrieval bot. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Add descriptive alt text to every image that carries information.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Give each informational image an alt attribute stating the fact it conveys ("Pro plan: $49 per user per month"), not a filename. Mark purely decorative images with alt="" so they are correctly skipped rather than left unlabelled.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves fact extractability by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

evidence_details.observation: 7 of 25 images (28%) have no alt attribute at all (images correctly marked decorative with alt="" are excluded). Any figure, price, spec or claim rendered inside those images is unreadable to a retrieval bot.

findings.severity_rationale: Rated low because the observed evidence indicates low impact; unavailable evidence is not treated as a defect.

proactive_recommendations.title: Mark up existing question-and-answer content with FAQPage schema
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already contains question-shaped content, but none of it is marked as FAQPage. FAQPage is the highest-leverage schema type for AI citation because its question/answer structure matches how retrieval systems chunk content and lift a quotable answer. The content already exists; only the markup is missing.

suggested_action.summary: Add FAQPage JSON-LD to pages that already answer common questions.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Wrap each question and its answer in FAQPage JSON-LD with mainEntity -> Question -> acceptedAnswer. Mark up the answers you already publish rather than writing new ones.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add Article schema with author and dateModified to editorial pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 1 crawled page(s) are editorial or documentation content carrying no Article schema. Authorship and a machine-readable modification date are the signals assistants use to decide whether a passage is current and attributable -- without them, an assistant that finds a good answer on the page still has no basis to date it or credit it.

suggested_action.summary: Mark editorial and documentation pages with Article JSON-LD.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add Article or TechArticle JSON-LD with headline, author (a Person or Organization with a real profile URL), datePublished and dateModified. Update dateModified when the content genuinely changes, not on every deploy.

proactive_recommendations.title: State AI usage terms explicitly in robots.txt
proactive_recommendations.rationale: robots.txt names which agents may crawl but says nothing about what may be done with the content once fetched. Emerging conventions -- Cloudflare's Content Signals Policy (released CC0) and RSL licensing terms -- let a publisher separate training use from search indexing and answer generation in machine-readable form, instead of leaving that distinction to be inferred from which user agents happen to be listed.

suggested_action.summary: Add machine-readable content-usage signals to robots.txt.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a Content Signals Policy block declaring your position on search, ai-input and ai-train separately, or publish RSL licensing terms. Keep it consistent with the agents you actually allow, or the two signals will contradict each other.

proactive_recommendations.title: Expose an agent-facing endpoint (NLWeb / MCP) built on existing structured data
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already publishes structured data, which is the input NLWeb uses to serve a conversational endpoint that AI agents can query directly rather than scraping HTML. Because it builds on schema.org markup, sitemaps and feeds you already maintain, it is incremental rather than a rebuild, and it moves the brand from being read by agents to being queryable by them.

suggested_action.summary: Evaluate an NLWeb instance exposing an /ask and /mcp endpoint over existing content.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Point an NLWeb instance at your existing schema.org data and sitemap, and expose /ask and /mcp. Start with the content an agent is most likely to be asked about -- catalogue, docs, pricing.

proactive_recommendations.title: Consider publishing llms.txt, with realistic expectations
proactive_recommendations.rationale: No /llms.txt is published. Be aware this is a low-evidence convention rather than an established standard: 2026 measurements find major AI crawlers almost never request the file, and Google has stated it has no effect on Search or AI Overviews. It costs very little to publish and may matter if uptake improves, but it should be treated as optionality -- not as a substitute for the structured data and third-party presence that demonstrably drive citation today.

suggested_action.summary: Optionally publish /llms.txt, after the higher-leverage items above.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: If you publish one, keep it to a short markdown index of your canonical product, docs, pricing and company pages, and keep it in sync with the site. Do not deprioritise schema work for it.
